trajectory supervision constrain complementary spatial distinctions.
Causal Replay combines them in shared parameters. The illustrated readouts
span categorical, metric, temporal, and reference-frame queries.

were both the bathtub and the folded towel on the observer’s left?
Q2 (Round 5): using the Round-2 facing as forward, did the observer move

Figure 4:Historical context in spatial reasoning.The first question retrieves an earlier state in which the bathtub
and folded towel lie on the observer’s left. The second evaluates
a later location relative to the facing direction in Round 2.
Teal indicates annotated states, and red shows the control’s
incorrect retrieval or displacement. Both questions depend on
a reference established earlier in the episode.

Figure 5:First appearance and category order.In scene1mp3d_0067_region16, ChronoReplay returns Round 3 for the first
appearance of the toilet and the order door, shelf, toilet paper. The matched
origin-shifted control returns Round 1 and reverses the latter two categories.
The early white fixture is a bidet; the toilet is partially visible at the
lower-right edge of the final Round 3 frame.

Figure 6:Historical retrieval and rotation.In sceneValidation_42898818, the Round 5 question asks which
round contained both the plant and sink; ChronoReplay returns Round 2,
whereas the control returns Round 4. A Round 7 question defines the
Round 1 facing as the orientation reference and specifies a rotation below180∘180^{\circ}. ChronoReplay correctly returns counterclockwise, while the
control returns clockwise.

Figure 7:Reference displacement and nearest-state retrieval.In scenescene0496_00, ChronoReplay identifies leftward displacement
relative to the Round 1 facing, while the control answers right. When asked
in Round 4 for the closest blackboard state, ChronoReplay retrieves Round 2
rather than the control’s Round 4. Left/right denotes displacement, not
turning direction; the closest-state label follows the source annotation
rather than apparent object size in a single image.

Figure 8:Two native interfaces on one mirror history.Selected chronological observations precede a left/right judgement and a
horizontal-distance estimate. Round labels identify the source observation turns. Base, Preservation, Trajectory, and Joint replay
use the same observations at each query endpoint. Joint retains the correct
direction; Trajectory has slightly lower absolute distance error, and both
tie at 0.70 under the official metric.

Figure 9:A fixed-observation global-layout failure.The official Base chooses B and ChronoReplay chooses D on OVO-S L4.3.
The upper panel shows eight timestamped frames from their shared Uniform-128
input. The lower panels reproduce the two source option diagrams in their
original orientations, with enlarged labels beside the key objects.
Captions describe positions within these diagrams.
The fireplace and table placements make the disagreement visible.
